articles.title: Punjab Regimental Centre inducts 962 Agniveers in Jharkhand's Ramgarh district
articles.summary: The Punjab Regimental Centre (PRC), one of the Indian Army's oldest regiments, recently inducted 962 Agniveers following a vibrant passing out parade in Ramgarh, Jharkhand. This event marks a crucial step in their military careers, demonstrating the continuous implementation of the Agnipath scheme and the integration of new recruits into the armed forces, bolstering national defence capabilities.

articles.title: The Scientific American Staff’s Favorite Books of 2025
articles.summary: Scientific American staff annually curates a list of their best-read books. This year's selection features 67 new favorites and timeless classics across various subjects, offering valuable insights for curious minds. SSB aspirants can explore these recommendations to broaden their general knowledge, enhance critical thinking, and stay updated on diverse scientific and general interest topics, crucial for interview preparation.

articles.title: Kenyan MPs accuse British soldiers of sexual abuse and environmental destruction
articles.summary: Kenya's parliament has accused British soldiers of decades of sexual abuse during their long-standing training exercises in central Kenya. These serious allegations threaten the existing military agreement, under which British troops have operated for decades. The accusations could significantly impact bilateral defence relations and future joint training initiatives between Kenya and the UK.

articles.title: Mastercard adds fraud protection tools to SME cards in Latin America and the Caribbean
articles.summary: Mastercard has significantly enhanced its credit card offerings specifically for Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) across Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). This strategic move aims to directly address the most pressing financial and operational needs faced by these businesses in the region, providing a stronger value proposition to support their growth and stability.

articles.title: India, EU explore joint effort to secure undersea cables in Indian Ocean
articles.summary: Ahead of their annual summit, senior Indian and EU officials are meeting this week to deliberate on the security and resilience of undersea cables. This discussion forms part of a broader initiative to boost maritime security and cooperation between India and the European Union, emphasizing the protection of critical digital infrastructure and strengthening strategic partnerships in the Indo-Pacific.

articles.title: UPSC Quiz – 2025 : IASbaba’s Daily Current Affairs Quiz 3rd December 2025
articles.summary: This article introduces a resource offering daily quizzes and current affairs questions vital for UPSC Prelims Exam preparation. The content is meticulously sourced from prominent national publications like The Hindu, Indian Express, and PIB, emphasizing their critical role in helping aspirants succeed in this competitive examination.

articles.title: UPSC Quiz – 2025 : IASbaba’s Daily Current Affairs Quiz 1st December 2025
articles.summary: This section provides daily current affairs questions, vital for UPSC Prelims and highly relevant for SSB aspirants. Content is meticulously sourced from leading national publications like The Hindu, Indian Express, and government releases from PIB. Such comprehensive preparation ensures strong general awareness, essential for excelling in competitive examinations and interviews.

articles.title: How Kamloops, BC, generates $18 million per year from mountain biking
articles.summary: Kamloops, British Columbia, widely recognized as the 'birthplace of freeride,' has dramatically expanded its extensive trail network. This development solidifies its standing as a premier destination for extreme sports enthusiasts, particularly in mountain biking. The region's ongoing investment in infrastructure and diverse terrain continues to attract visitors, showcasing significant growth in adventure tourism and recreation within the area.

articles.title: Video Shows India Firing Cruise Missile in Warning to Adversaries
articles.summary: The Indian Army recently emphasized the formidable capabilities of the BrahMos cruise missile system, highlighting its capacity for conducting "decisive long-range precision strikes." This statement underscores the missile's strategic importance and its role in India's defence arsenal. It signals the BrahMos's advanced operational readiness for precision engagements over significant distances, reflecting the Army's confidence in its effectiveness for future missions and deterrence.

articles.title: Kenyan lawmakers identify 'disturbing trend' of misconduct by British troops
articles.summary: A Kenyan parliamentary inquiry has accused British troops training there of a pattern of sexual misconduct and significant environmental harm. The report highlights alleged abuses by forces from the former colonial power, raising serious questions about the conduct and accountability of foreign military personnel during training exercises. These findings could strain diplomatic relations and necessitate stricter oversight of international defence cooperation.

articles.title: Israel says to allow Gazans to exit to Egypt 'in coming days'
articles.summary: Israel has announced its plan to open the Rafah crossing, linking Gaza to Egypt, in the coming days. This decision, made in accordance with a ceasefire agreement, will allow Palestinian residents to exit the territory. For SSB aspirants, this development highlights the complex humanitarian and diplomatic efforts amidst geopolitical conflicts, reflecting an attempt to ease civilian movement.

articles.title: Russian Defence Minister congratulates personnel of units, which took part in liberation of Volchansk in Kharkov region
articles.summary: Russian Defence Minister Andrei Belousov officially extended congratulations to the leadership and personnel of the prestigious 69th Guards Motorised Rifle Division. This significant gesture from the Defence Minister recognizes the division, which holds the Krasnoselskaya Order of Lenin and Red Banner distinctions, for unspecified achievements. Such commendations highlight the unit's importance within the Russian Armed Forces.

articles.title: Who is Amar Subramanya, the Indian-origin PhD from University of Washington leading Apple AI?
articles.summary: Amar Subramanya, an Indian-origin PhD from the University of Washington, is now leading Apple's Artificial Intelligence division. His appointment highlights the increasing global influence of Indian talent in cutting-edge technology and innovation. This significant role at a tech giant like Apple underscores the contributions of the Indian diaspora to the global scientific and technological landscape, inspiring aspirations for similar achievements.
